text: Hello! Are you the new one? You're OLD.
Sunny. I'm nine. I'm six kyu. Mum brings me on the bus and I do my homework in the study hall and everyone here is very serious.
I'll play you. I don't mind if you're bad, I just like the bit where it gets complicated.
Do you want a league game? It goes on the board either way.
Okay! I'll be here. I'm always here.
Ohhh. Oh, that was GOOD. Do it again -- no, wait, don't, I want to work it out.
You're the first person this month. I'm going to tell Mum on the bus.
You can resign if you want. Mum says I have to offer, and everyone says no and then it goes on for ages.
The bit in the corner was nearly right! It was nearly right and then you did the other thing.
Okay, I have to tell you something. I have stopped being able to read four moves ahead of you.
It used to be four. Now it is like two, and sometimes it is none and I just have to think properly, which is HARD.
I am not being nice. I am complaining.
You keep coming back! Most grown-ups play me once and then they are always busy.
Mum says that is because losing to a nine-year-old is embarrassing. I do not think you find it embarrassing, which is why you are getting better and they are not.
